title: Do paved roads pay for themselves? Evidence from Rwanda
summary: A study of Rwanda's road paving programme finds that infrastructure investment substantially boosts local tax revenues, driven by small, informal firm entry and rising rental values, while central tax collections remain unchanged.

title: Can coastal fishing zones protect Africa's artisanal fishers?
summary: New radar data shows that protected nearshore fishing zones can successfully keep industrial vessels out of African coastal waters, boosting fish stocks and small-scale catches without cutting industrial fishing overall.

title: Masculinity norms and their economic implications, explained

title: China's nationwide carbon market: Costs, environmental gains, and potential reforms
summary: China’s carbon market is projected to deliver benefits well in excess of its cost – and smarter benchmark and auction design could make it even more effective.

summary: Exposure to fine particulate matter during cognitive assessments lowered adult cognitive performance in Kenya, and coarser pollution measures missed much of this short-run variation.

title: Does asking communities to contribute to development projects improve impact and cost-effectiveness?

title: Should workers or managers decide who gets rewarded?
